name: Ogbono Soup
summary: A silky, slippery draw soup made from ground wild mango seeds, palm oil, crayfish and meat.
story: Ogbono soup is made from the ground seeds of the wild African mango, which gives it a distinctive slippery, drawing texture. It is a common family and party dish across southern Nigeria, usually eaten with a swallow like eba, fufu or pounded yam. Cooks often add okra or leaves to vary it.

items.name: Ground dried pepper or fresh scotch bonnet

steps.title: Cook the meat
steps.text: Boil the meat with onion, a stock cube and salt until tender, adding stockfish near the end. Keep all the stock, you will need around 3 cups.

steps.title: Melt the palm oil
steps.text: Place the palm oil in a pot over low heat just until it melts and becomes clear, about 1 to 2 minutes. Do not boil it.

steps.title: Cream the ogbono
steps.text: Add the ground ogbono to the oil and stir with a wooden spoon to make a smooth thick paste. Cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes until it loosens and smells nutty.

steps.title: Add stock slowly
steps.text: Pour in the warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until the soup is smooth with no lumps. Keep the heat low to medium.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add crayfish, pepper, meat and fish. Cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then so it does not stick; it should draw into stretchy strings from the spoon.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the greens if using and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Adjust salt and thin with a little stock or hot water if too thick.

tips: Cream the ogbono in oil first; dropping it into hot liquid makes lumps.
Keep the heat low. High heat makes the soup stick and burn at the bottom.
Add stock gradually to control the thickness.

swaps.swap: There is no true substitute; for a different draw soup use okra, but flavour and texture will change.
Vegetable oil works but the colour and flavour will be milder.
